forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Dacorum forecasts £22.393m full-year deficit, £99k above budget; Paradise Depot scheme £1.5m over
news_drafts.lead:
Dacorum Borough Council's first-quarter budget monitoring (the in-year check of spending against budget), presented to Cabinet on 6 October, forecasts a full-year deficit on the provision of services of £22.393m against a budgeted £22.294m, a difference of £99k. The year-to-date position was £8.917m favourable.

The largest single variance is in capital spending (money spent on things that last). The Paradise Depot housing scheme, paid for from the housing revenue account (the ring-fenced account for the council's own homes, funded by rents), has a current budget of £7.2m, including £2.5m slipped from the previous year. It is forecast to cost £8.7m, £1.5m more, with £926k spent so far. The Hub community facility and foodbank scheme was given £352k in-year, taking its budget to £1m, but is forecast to cost £1.2m, £180k over, with £139k spent.

Within the housing revenue account, responsive repairs are forecast to overspend by about £200k, currently offset by an underspend on disrepair compensation claims. Officers are reviewing whether this is temporary or a continuing trend, with findings expected in the coming weeks. In Environment, parking income is £177k ahead of forecast, against garage income £136k and cesspool income £56k short, leaving a net £15k overspend.

news_drafts.headline: Dacorum housing depot project £1.5m over budget as capital delivery falters
news_drafts.lead: Dacorum council faces a £1.5m overspend on the Paradise Depot, a housing repairs scheme budgeted at £7.2m but now projected to cost £8.7m — a 21% overspend and the largest single capital overspend in the entire programme. Work is well underway with nearly £1m already spent. The overspend comes as the council's housing investment programme more broadly stutters: a scheme to build new council homes budgeted at £4.4m is now forecast to spend only £1m this year, a 77 per cent shortfall. Meanwhile, the council has discovered the Forum's electricity meter was faulty for years; repair work completed in April means annual utility bills will jump by £200k. The findings emerged from the Finance and Resources scrutiny committee's review of quarter-one spending.

findings.committee: Finance and Resources Overview and Scrutiny
findings.paper_title: OSC Q2 Financial Monitoring Report - updated version
findings.headline: HRA income expected to contribute a £371k surplus from low void rates on HRA stock.
findings.detail: The surplus holds if strong occupancy continues through the year. Emergency accommodation for vulnerable residents, provided from HRA stock, is also generating circa £356k of income from the General Fund.
findings.matters: Using HRA stock for General Fund emergency accommodation creates an intra-council income flow that other councils with similar homelessness pressures may also rely on.
findings.figures: £371k surplus; circa £356k from General Fund; HRA income variance £452k above budget (Table 5)
findings.quote: Strong HRA income performance continues to be driven by low void rates for HRA stock, which is expected to contribute a surplus of £371k

findings.committee: Finance and Resources Overview and Scrutiny
findings.paper_title: OSC Q2 Financial Monitoring Report - updated version
findings.headline: Increased electricity costs at The Forum forecast at £200k.
findings.detail: The paper lists this as one of the notable General Fund pressures alongside the Planning Service, Trees & Woodlands works and the Revenues & Benefits funding shortfall. No further detail is given on the cause.
findings.matters: Energy cost increases at council-run leisure and civic buildings affect many councils' revenue budgets and their energy procurement decisions.
findings.quote: increased electricity costs at The Forum (£200k)

findings.committee: Finance and Resources Overview and Scrutiny
findings.paper_title: OSC Q2 Financial Monitoring Report - updated version
findings.headline: £3.368m of £3.487m savings reported on track, with £103k of garage rental income and £16k of garden waste delayed.
findings.detail: The garage rental income delay follows a Quarter 1 forecast of £136k below target because of rising void rates. This is largely offset by an expected £142k underspend on garage planned maintenance. The garden waste delay may be met by in-year receipts.
findings.matters: A savings tracker with most of its target on track, and the remaining gaps named, shows how a council is monitoring delivery of its budget savings.
findings.figures: £3.487m total savings; £3.368m on track; £16k garden waste delayed; £103k garage rental delayed; £136k Quarter 1 garage income shortfall; £142k garage maintenance underspend
findings.quote: Of the £3.487m of savings, £3.368m are deemed to be on track.

findings.committee: Finance and Resources Overview and Scrutiny
findings.paper_title: OSC Q2 Financial Monitoring Report - updated version
findings.headline: Repairs & Maintenance budgets forecast a £288k pressure at Quarter 2, mainly from fire safety equipment works.
findings.detail: Officers are reviewing expenditure with analysis from Cardo to see whether the increase is temporary or sustained. Where ongoing pressures are identified, the paper says officers will consider mitigations and feed resourcing needs into the HRA Business Planning process.
findings.matters: Fire safety compliance costs in the HRA are a live cost pressure for social housing landlords, and the review outcome will affect the HRA business plan.
findings.quote: Repairs & Maintenance budgets are forecast to experience a £288k pressure at Quarter 2

findings.committee: Finance and Resources Overview and Scrutiny
findings.paper_title: OSC Q2 Financial Monitoring Report - updated version
findings.headline: Internal borrowing rate charged by the General Fund to the HRA increased from 3.5% to 4.0% from October.
findings.detail: The increase benefits the General Fund, and the paper says it strengthens the General Fund forecast. It increases the forecast HRA pressure from £395k at Quarter 1 to £544k at Quarter 2. The change is intended to align the rate with average investment returns in the Treasury Management Strategy.
findings.matters: Internal borrowing rates between a General Fund and HRA move cost between the two accounts, and other councils' HRA business plans will be affected by any similar rate change.
findings.figures: 3.5% to 4.0%; HRA pressure increased by £149k, from £395k to £544k
findings.quote: from October onwards the interest rate charged by the General Fund to the HRA for internal borrowing used to finance the HRA Capital Programme has increased from 3.5% to 4.0%
